tools.name: deploy_site
tools.description: Publishes files as a new website at a share link and returns its URL. Each call creates a separate site at a new URL; update_site changes an existing one. Limits: 200 files and 4 MB in total. The result includes a site_id and a manage_token that the other site tools require. Anyone with the URL can

tools.name: update_site
tools.description: Replaces the content of an existing site with the given files, at the same URL. The files are the complete new version, not a patch: anything left out is no longer served. The previous version is kept and rollback_site restores it.

tools.name: rollback_site
tools.description: Makes an earlier version of a site live again at the same URL. With no version_id it restores the version before the current one. get_site lists the versions available.

tools.name: get_site
tools.description: Returns a site's URL, name, when it expires, which version is live, and its version history.

tools.name: compare_versions
tools.description: Lists the files added, removed and modified between two versions of a site. With no arguments beyond the site it compares the live version with the one before it.

tools.name: duplicate_site
tools.description: Copies a temporary site's live content to a new site at a new URL, leaving the original untouched. The copy is temporary and comes with its own site_id and manage_token. A site that belongs to an account cannot be duplicated this way.

tools.name: configure_timeline
tools.description: Shows or hides a History chip on the site's pages that lets any visitor open its earlier versions and compare two of them, which is useful while a site is being reviewed. Off by default. When it is on, the result includes a history_url that shows two versions side by side, and get_site lists a url f

tools.name: protect_site
tools.description: Makes a site private behind a password (flypod Pro), or shows its password again. With enabled true and no password, flypod makes a strong one (four words and a number) if the site has none, and otherwise keeps it. The result has the password, a share_url that opens the site without typing, and a cu

tools.name: configure_domain
tools.description: Connects a custom domain such as www.example.com to a site (flypod Pro). The result names the person's DNS provider, the one record to add in that provider's own field names, a link to the page where it is added, and `say`: the same steps in one plain sentence for the person. tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: Lists the sites that belong to the flypod account this connector is signed in to, with each site's URL and name.

tools.name: keep_site
tools.description: Attaches a temporary site to the signed-in flypod account so it no longer expires. The URL does not change. Requires the connector to be signed in; otherwise the person can use the keep_url from deploy_site.

tools.name: rename_site
tools.description: Sets the display name of a site on the account page. The URL does not change. An empty name clears it.

tools.name: delete_site
tools.description: Permanently deletes a site that belongs to the signed-in account: its URL stops working and every version is removed. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: upgrade_plan
tools.description: Returns a payment link for flypod Pro: custom domains, password-protected sites, and higher limits on deploys, storage and updates per hour. The person pays on that page themselves (card, Apple Pay or Google Pay; about 30 seconds); calling this tool charges nothing. Once they have paid, the account

tools.name: configure_comments
tools.description: Enables or disables visitor comments on a site and sets who may comment: `anonymous` (anyone), `passcode` (anyone with the shared passcode), or `approved` (comments appear after the owner approves them). Disabling keeps existing comments. Only the site's owner can change this.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: Lists the comment threads on a site, each with the text it is attached to, its status and its first comment. Also reports whether comments are enabled and in which mode.

tools.name: get_comment_thread
tools.description: Returns one comment thread with every reply.

tools.name: post_comment
tools.description: Starts a comment thread on a page of a site, attached to a passage of its text. `quote` has to be text that appears on the page exactly as written there.

tools.name: reply_to_comment
tools.description: Adds a reply to an existing comment thread.

tools.name: update_comment_thread
tools.description: Changes the state of a comment thread: `resolve` marks it done, `reopen` undoes that, and `approve` or `reject` decide a thread waiting in the moderation queue (owner only).

tools.name: delete_comment_thread
tools.description: Deletes a comment thread. Allowed for the thread's author and for the site's owner.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: deploy_site, get_site, configure_timeline, list_sites, list_comments, get_comment_thread · Private data: deploy_site, update_site, compare_versions, protect_site, configure_domain, upgrade_plan · Public sink: deploy_site, post_comment · Destructive: configure_domain, delete_site, delete_comment_thread.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: deploy_site, get_site, configure_timeline, list_sites, list_comments, get_comment_thread · Private data: deploy_site, update_site, compare_versions, protect_site, configure_domain, upgrade_plan · Public sink: deploy_site, post_comment · Destructive: configure_domain, delete_site, delete_comment_thread

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
